newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey still inspecting U.S. wheat cargo.
newsitem.headline: Turkey still inspecting U.S. wheat cargo.

text.p: Turkish farm quarantine officials are still inspecting a cargo of 15,000 tonnes of U.S. milling wheat for ergot fungus and no decision on whether to reject it has been made, Agriculture Minister Musa Demirci said on Monday.
"Wheat imported from the United States is still being inspected against ergot fungus at our Tekirdag and Kocaeli (Derince) customs depots," Demirci said in a statement.

"The inspection is being made to see whether the wheat meets tolerable limits in terms of ergot fungus and it is completely out of the question that any U.S. wheat has so far been rejected or its entrance (to Turkey) has been denied," he said.
"The wheat held at customs depots will be allowed if they meet the allowable limits defined by international and national legislations," he said.

Turkey held the U.S. milling wheat cargo two weeks ago on the grounds that it contained ergot fungus which failed to meet its zero-tolerance limit defined in the country's Farm Quarantine Act, actually designed for seed wheat only.
But Turkish farmers, traders and millers as well as U.S. officials have said no country in the world can guarantee a zero-tolerance for ergot fungus.
Another piece of Turkish legislation, the Food Act, allows 0.1 percent of ergot in imported wheat.
Traders and millers said the agricultural ministry was mistakenly applying the Food Quarantine Act on imported milling wheat instead of the Food Act.
They said some 100,000 tonnes of milling wheat, including grain presently being held, were heading for Turkey from the United States.
